reasoning: A fixed-point transformation partitions positions and values into the same consecutive blocks. Each block is one permutation cycle and begins with its largest value; a block of size s>=2 has(s-2)! possibilities. Count compositions with these block weights, then unrank by the first block maximum. Within a block, assign remaining permutation entries lexicographically while disallowing a premature cycle: partial edges form disjoint directed paths, and joining the remaining path components into one cycle has a factorial number of completions. DSU detects premature closure; the final edge is allowed to close the full cycle. Exact integers avoid saturation errors for ranks up to10^18.
